an3.76:1.2: “Continued existence” (_bhava_, cf. “being”) is the “life” or “plane of existence” in which one is born as an ongoing series of manifestations of the aggregates. It includes both the active aspects of life (defilements and deeds) as well as the resultant body and mind. Consider it by analogy with, say, visiting a park. First there is the spark of an idea, a vague impression of a “park” in the mind, which solidifies into an intention. Acting on it, one goes to the park, where it becomes one’s reality, the “world” one inhabits. Likewise, by creating ideas and volitions in the mind, one is aligning or tuning into the corresponding realm of existence, priming the mind to project itself into that state and make it a reality when one is reborn there. The deeds that determine rebirth in a state of existence shape the baseline experience in that state. Since the deed is of necessity limited in power, the resultant state must be impermanent.
an3.76:2.1: “Deeds to result in the sensual realm” are volitional actions whose motivations, bound by desire, are primed for rebirth in one of the sensual realms, namely: hell, the animal realm, the domain of the forefathers, the human realm, or any of the heavenly realms below the realms of divinity. This includes morally potent choices, good or bad, in all states of mind except absorption.
an3.76:2.3: The metaphor of agriculture, which is applied elsewhere (eg. [an3.34:13.6]()), is fundamental to the conception of rebirth as a process that is both organic and purposeful. Sowing seeds requires sacrifice; one restrains from consuming the food now, in the belief that even more food will be produced in the future. In the same way, one who is aware of kamma will restrain themselves from actions of immediate gratification for the sake of abundant future welfare. | “Deeds are the field” (_kammaṁ khettaṁ_): the field is the land on which the work of agriculture is done. | “Consciousness is the seed” (_viññāṇaṁ bījaṁ_): consciousness conveys the information needed for a new life. | “Craving is the moisture” (_taṇhā sneho_): _taṇhā_ and _sneha_ are synonyms, both being shades of “desire”. But they are also opposites, since _taṇhā_ is “thirst” while _sneha_ is “moisture”.
an3.76:2.4: The phrase “shrouded by ignorance” describes beings roaming through transmigration ([sn15.1](), [iti14]()). _Nīvaraṇa_ ultimately stems from Vṛtra, the serpent who, by coiling around the mountain, both “shrouded” it in darkness, and “hindered” or blocked it. | Consciousness is “established” like a seed is planted. | The sensual realm is “lower” (_hīna_) than the realms of divinity, even though it includes many fortunate existences such as the human realm.
an3.76:3.1: “Luminous form” is _rūpa_. Here this is a technical term for the radiant perception of light in which one in absorption is immersed.
an3.76:3.4: The purified consciousness of absorption results in rebirth in one of the realms of divinity, here called “middle”.
an3.76:4.1: These are the realms corresponding to the four formless attainments which surpass the absorptions.
an3.76:4.4: The Buddha’s argument is that, although the higher realms appear greatly different, in the end they are part of the same process, following the same fundamental principles. This is why he rejected the path of his former teachers, as it leads only to rebirth in the formless realms ([mn26:15.35]()).
